title: Go-style duration parser
prompt: Implement a header-only function `std::optional<std::chrono::nanoseconds> parse_duration(std::string_view text)` in the global namespace that parses Go-style duration strings.
Grammar: an optional sign ('+' or '-') followed by one or more `<number><unit>` pairs with no separators or whitespace.
- A number is decimal digits with an optional fractional part: "1", "1.5", ".5" and "5." are valid; there must be at least one digit.
- Units: "ns", "us", "µs" (U+00B5 MICRO SIGN, UTF-8), "μs" (U+03BC GREEK SMALL LETTER MU, UTF-8), "ms", "s", "m", "h".
- The string "0" (optionally signed) is valid and means zero. Any other number without a unit is invalid.
- Units may repeat and appear in any order ("1h1h" is two hours).
- Fractions are truncated toward zero at nanosecond precision ("1.9999999999s" is 1999999999ns).
- The result must fit in a signed 64-bit count of nanoseconds; "-9223372036854775808ns" is valid, anything outside the range is invalid.
- Return std::nullopt for any invalid input: empty string, lone sign, unknown unit, missing unit, whitespace, malformed number, or overflow.
